Split each actor's sequence into phases

Source: R/mark_phases.R
mark_phases.Rd

mark_phases() divides the events of each actor into n consecutive phases of nearly equal length and records the phase of every event in a new column. The result can be passed to build_network() with group = "phase" to estimate one network per phase, for example to compare the first and second halves of each session.

The events of an actor are ordered by time (or kept in row order) and numbered \(k = 1, \dots, L\). Event \(k\) belongs to phase \(\lceil k n / L \rceil\), so the phases of one actor differ in length by at most one event, and with an odd number of events and n = 2 the middle event belongs to the second phase. An actor with fewer than n events has no events in some phases.

Usage

mark_phases(
  data,
  actor = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  n = 2L,
  labels = NULL,
  name = "phase"
)

Arguments

data

An event log: a data frame with one row per event.

actor

The column identifying whose events form one sequence (a session, a student). Default NULL, which treats the whole log as one sequence.

time

The column ordering the events within each actor: numeric, a Date or a POSIXct. Default NULL, which keeps the row order.

n

The number of phases, a whole number of at least 2. Default 2.

labels

The labels of the phases, in order, n distinct non-empty strings. Default NULL, which uses "1", "2", ..., "n".

name

The name of the new column. Default "phase". A column of that name already in data raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

Value

data with one added character column, name, holding each event's phase label; the rows and the other columns are unchanged and keep their order. An absent actor or time column, missing values in either, a time column of another type, or an invalid n or labels raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

See also

build_network() for the per-phase networks, sequence_compare() and permutation() for comparing them.

Examples

halves <- mark_phases(human_long, actor = "session_id",
                      time = "order_in_session", n = 2,
                      labels = c("early", "late"))
head(halves)
#>   message_id   project   session_id  timestamp session_date      code
#> 1       3439 Project_7 0086cabebd15 1772661600   2026-03-05   Specify
#> 2       3439 Project_7 0086cabebd15 1772661600   2026-03-05   Command
#> 3       3439 Project_7 0086cabebd15 1772661600   2026-03-05   Specify
#> 4       3440 Project_7 0086cabebd15 1772661600   2026-03-05 Interrupt
#> 5       3442 Project_7 0086cabebd15 1772661600   2026-03-05    Verify
#> 6       3444 Project_7 0086cabebd15 1772661600   2026-03-05   Specify
#>         cluster code_order order_in_session phase
#> 1     Directive          1                1 early
#> 2     Directive          2                2 early
#> 3     Directive          3                3 early
#> 4 Metacognitive          1                4 early
#> 5    Evaluative          1                7 early
#> 6     Directive          1               10 early
net <- build_network(halves, method = "relative", actor = "session_id",
                     action = "cluster", time = "order_in_session",
                     group = "phase")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (2 sessions), 'code' (125 sessions)
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (2 sessions), 'code' (114 sessions)
net
